chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muthanna from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Hajj is in known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. No one may enter the state of Ihram for Hajj in any other time, and no one may enter Ihram before the time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The example of this is like one who prays four rak'ahs during travel and leaves the two (rak'ahs).

key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the specific months for Hajj and when should one enter Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes these narrations to clarify the distinction between the general prohibition of early Ihram and specific exceptions for voluntary vows (nadhr) or fear of missing the month of Rajab for Umrah. The text highlights the scholarly preference for the 'easier' path (Yasir) in ritual practice, illustrating the principle that Allah loves simplicity and rewards adherence to the Sunnah over unnecessary hardship.
